subject: Why aren't you taking bismark cov/bedgraph instead?

messages.author: a6d6602cf396c303
messages.subject: Why aren't you taking bismark cov/bedgraph instead?
parts:
Hi,

I feel dreadful that you are taking in sam files for bismark instead of the post-processing files such as the bedgraph / cov files generated by bismark_methyl_extractor as input. 
Can you let me know if you are able to take in the post-processing files from bismark_methyl_extractor?

Thank you.

Wilson

messages.author: ab8277113f65c05e
messages.subject: Re: [methylkit_discussion] Why aren't you taking bismark cov/bedgraph instead?
parts:
you feel dreadful???  Please see this post. 
https://groups.google.com/d/msg/methylkit_discussion/nOk2hM439Ak/5HBB5jefadYJ

methylKit can deal with a variety of generic methylation ratio/percentage files. However, bismark output doesn't have enough information without extra processing which can be done via awk/perl or python. You can try to contact felix to add one more column to the bismark output so that it has minimal information we require. When we wrote methylKit Bismark didn't provide any bedgraph/coverage file and as demonstrated by blog posts in the link I sent we are able to read different types of files.

hope you are feeling less dreadful,
Best,
Altuna

messages.subject: Re: [methylkit_discussion] Why aren't you taking bismark cov/bedgraph instead?
parts:
Hi,

I see methylkit as potentially a very powerful tools to analyze RRBS data. Bismark has already came out with multi-threads methyl extraction script which can extract the methylation status from the bam files. It is very fast.
So, methylkit only uses the bam files from bismark as input. It is repeating the extraction step performed by bismark methyl extraction? And, slower? 
To make things less dreadful, can the author add one more input option which is to read processed output files from bismark methylation extractor?

Thank you.

Wilson

messages.author: ab8277113f65c05e
messages.subject: Re: [methylkit_discussion] Why aren't you taking bismark cov/bedgraph instead?
parts:
If you already have the files from Bismark bedgraph easiest thing is to process them to a format acceptable by methylkit (use perl, awk or python, should not take long to code). 

I haven't compared the speed but I know methylkit needs less memory and I suspect it is faster but it only works with sorted sam files not bam.

The author is busy at the moment but he may find time to implement this in the future, I think you should also ask Felix to add one more column to Bismark output. In addition, methylkit is open-source and developed through github and you can contribute to it. Start by opening an issue and discussing strategies on how to implement this feature if you would like to do that yourself. 

Best,
Altuna

messages.author: ab8277113f65c05e
messages.subject: Re: [methylkit_discussion] Why aren't you taking bismark cov/bedgraph instead?
parts:
some update on this:
Cytosine report seems to have uncovered positions as well. And the other files do not have strand information so they can not be imported to methylKit at all.

Even if I write something to import from cytosine report it will take too much time to read all the non-covered bases and filter them out later in R. The best is that user process them beforehand. While the user is processing the files to remove uncovered bases, it is trivial to also process the files to a format acceptable by methylKit. The following awk one-liner will do that, and convert the cytosine report from CpGs to a format readable by methylKit (https://groups.google.com/d/msg/methylkit_discussion/nOk2hM439Ak/5HBB5jefadYJ)

awk  '{OFS="\t";if($4+0 > 0 || $5+0 >0 ) print $1,$2,$3,$4/($4+$5),$4+$5;}' cytosineReport.txt > outputForMethylKit

this will give chr,start,strand, methylationRatio,coverage

messages.subject: Re: [methylkit_discussion] Why aren't you taking bismark cov/bedgraph instead?
parts: check bismark documentation.
On Thu, Apr 26, 2018 at 8:37 AM, <shuklas...@gmail.com> wrote:

Could you please suggest me how to make a cytosine report??

On Tuesday, November 11, 2014 at 5:00:40 PM UTC+5:30, Altuna Akalin wrote:

some update on this:
Cytosine report seems to have uncovered positions as well. And the other files do not have strand information so they can not be imported to methylKit at all.

Even if I write something to import from cytosine report it will take too much time to read all the non-covered bases and filter them out later in R. The best is that user process them beforehand. While the user is processing the files to remove uncovered bases, it is trivial to also process the files to a format acceptable by methylKit. The following awk one-liner will do that, and convert the cytosine report from CpGs to a format readable by methylKit (https://groups.google.com/d/msg/methylkit_discussion/nOk2hM439Ak/5HBB5jefadYJ)

awk  '{OFS="\t";if($4+0 > 0 || $5+0 >0 ) print $1,$2,$3,$4/($4+$5),$4+$5;}' cytosineReport.txt > outputForMethylKit

this will give chr,start,strand, methylationRatio,coverage
On Tue, Nov 11, 2014 at 11:42 AM, Kalyan K Pasumarthy <kaly...@gmail.com> wrote:

I have tried the newer methylKit extraction. It is pretty faster than the previous versions (atleast on RRBS dataset). One can use multiple cores now! Users who wish to speed up their analysis may chose native bismark methylkit extraction.

I have not assessed the usage of memory.

Regards,
Kalyan
On 11 November 2014 12:38, Altuna Akalin <aak...@gmail.com> wrote:

If you already have the files from Bismark bedgraph easiest thing is to process them to a format acceptable by methylkit (use perl, awk or python, should not take long to code). 

I haven't compared the speed but I know methylkit needs less memory and I suspect it is faster but it only works with sorted sam files not bam.

The author is busy at the moment but he may find time to implement this in the future, I think you should also ask Felix to add one more column to Bismark output. In addition, methylkit is open-source and developed through github and you can contribute to it. Start by opening an issue and discussing strategies on how to implement this feature if you would like to do that yourself. 

Best,
Altuna
